_note: The noticeboard on the Green (docs/15-regions.md, Noticeboards). The seed picks a writer's line and fills {where} from `spots` and {in} from `places`. Kinds: find, deliver, bring, thin (win 2 fights in a place), clear (win every fight listed for a place, 3 or more). `pay` is the least and most a notice of that kind may pay, in item worth; `npm run check` holds every payment to it. A place, a person or a spot joins by adding a row here. A writer must be in town at every hour, so the map's star is never wrong. A spot is an interactable that shows while its flag `spot:<id>` is set.
gearHint: It's plain work, mind. There's a fellow in a dark coat on the Green who knows what can be done with plain work. Don't say I said so.

words.thin: Clear two lots of creatures from {in}.
words.short: That isn't all of them. I said {of}.
words.blurb: A notice on the Green, from {name}. Pays {pay}.
words.fightBlurb: A notice on the Green, from {name}. Pays {pay}. Creatures already seen off come back after a rest.

posted.text: HARVEST FAIR. Tonight on the Green. Pie judging at six. Lanterns at dusk. Music by the Weller brothers.
LOST: grey cat, answers to Biscuit (sometimes). Last seen eating somebody's butter. Apply to A. Hale, whose butter it was.
LOST: grey cat. Someone has crossed out LOST and written, in Ada Hale's hand: UNFORTUNATELY NOT.
A faded card, marked with a rune of three crossed lines.

spots.where: in the hay by the quilt stall
by the gap in the orchard wall
by the old crate in the orchard
at the cairn in Brook Woods
under the fallen log in Brook Woods
by the mailbox on the south lane
at the scarecrow's feet in the south fields
where the path gives out in Alder Hollow

thanks: That'll do. Don't let it go to your head.
Good. Mind the step on your way out.
Well. I've had worse help, and paid more for it.

notices.title: A Belt on Account
notices.text: A belt came in against an account nobody has paid. See off two lots in {in} and it's yours, and I'll call the matter closed.

notices.title: Ada's Scoop
notices.text: Lost the good scoop {where}. Don't ask me how it got there. Biscuit, I expect.

notices.title: An Account Book
notices.text: My account book has turned up, I'm told, {where}. Bring it back and I won't read out what's in it.

notices.title: Paid For
notices.got: From Ada? I've been busy. Tell her I've been busy.
notices.text: Parcel for Silas Pike, paid for and not collected. He says he has been busy. He has not been busy. Walk it over and I'll call it square.

notices.title: Two Weeks Late
notices.got: Two weeks. You may tell Ada I counted.
notices.text: Martha Combs's thread came in. Two weeks late, so she'll say something. Take it over and let her say it to you.

notices.title: Butter Keeping
notices.text: Buying rime shards, three. They keep the butter better than the cellar does, and they don't eat any of it.

notices.title: Quills, Bought
notices.text: Buying burrback quills, two. They make a good pen and a better argument.

notices.title: Teeth Marks
notices.text: Something in {in} has been at my deliveries. I've had a crate left on the step with teeth marks in it. Two lots want seeing off.

notices.title: Not Safe, I'm Told
notices.text: I've been told {in} isn't safe for a delivery. I would like to be told otherwise. All of it, mind. Then come and tell me.

thanks: Hm. Don't tell Ada I paid you.

notices.title: Something for the Pocket
notices.text: Two lots in {in} have been at my windfalls. See them off and you can have what I found in the press last fall. No idea what it's for. It has done me no harm.

notices.title: Frost-Bit
notices.text: Want three frost-bit apples. Yes, frost-bit. Don't ask what for and I won't tell Ada. Leave off any with worms.

notices.title: The Press Pin
notices.text: Dropped the press pin {where}. Forty years I never lost one. Bring it back and we'll say no more.

notices.title: A Cider Bung
notices.text: My bung went off the last cart and landed {where}, the driver says. I want it. They don't make that size.

notices.title: Don't Shake It
notices.got: Silas sent this? It's been shaken.
notices.text: Jug to go to Martha Combs. Don't shake it. Don't sample it. I'll know.

notices.title: Paid, In Full
notices.got: Paid, is it. We'll see about that.
notices.text: Ada wants her bill paid. Here it is, paid. Put it in her hand and leave before she counts it.

notices.title: The Windfalls
notices.text: Something in {in} keeps getting into the windfalls. Two lots, about. See them off and I'll stand you a cider or two.

notices.title: My Own Reasons
notices.text: I want {in} clear. All of it. I've told nobody why and I won't start now.

thanks: There. That wasn't so hard, was it?
Thank you. You've a hole in that sleeve, you know.
I'd have done it myself, if I'd had the time. Take this.

notices.title: A Card of Needles
notices.text: Dropped a card of needles {where}. They were my mother's, and I would know if you kept one.

notices.title: My Good Shears
notices.text: My good shears have gone off and been left {where}. I don't ask who borrowed them. I will find out.

notices.title: One Shirt, Mended
notices.got: Saved the collar, did she? Tell her my father wore that collar.
notices.text: Amos Tuttle's shirt, mended. Tell him the collar was past saving and I saved it.

notices.title: Socks, Again
notices.got: Socks. I didn't ask for socks. I'm glad of them, mind.
notices.text: Jonah Reed's socks, darned. Again. Tell him a foot isn't meant to go through there.

notices.title: Buttons, Any
notices.text: Wanted: three copper buttons, for a coat. They needn't match. The coat doesn't.

notices.title: The Drying Line
notices.text: Something in {in} got at my drying line. I counted two lots before I came in. Frozen sheets stand up by themselves and I'd rather they didn't.

notices.title: Of a Sunday
notices.text: I used to walk to {in} of a Sunday, and I mean to again. Clear the lot, if you would. I'll know if you skipped any.

notices.title: My Brother's Coat
notices.text: My brother's coat is still on the peg. He isn't coming back for it and I've stopped mending it. See off two lots in {in}, where he cut wood, and it's yours.

writers.signed: A. Tuttle, the house with the clock
thanks: Obliged. My father would've said so too, at more length.
Well now. That's a thing done.
Good. I'd have got to it. Here.

notices.title: A Good Pipe
notices.text: Left my good pipe {where}. I'm not walking there twice for it. Somebody's legs are younger than mine.

notices.title: My Spectacles
notices.text: My spectacles are {where}. I set them down to look at something, and then I couldn't see what.

notices.title: Exact Money
notices.got: It's short. It's always short. Tell him I said so.
notices.text: Clock oil money owed to Ada Hale. Exact. She can count it herself and tell me it's short, as her mother did.

notices.title: A Borrowed Wrench
notices.got: His father had that off mine. I'd given it up.
notices.text: Silas Pike's father lent my father a wrench. Here it is. I don't say it was quick.

notices.title: For the Works
notices.text: Three rime shards, for a matter of the clock. It runs better cold than I like to admit.

notices.title: Every Autumn
notices.text: My father walked {in} every autumn and never met a thing. Now they tell me there's creatures in it. Two lots seen off would be a start.

notices.title: A Walk, Once
notices.text: Time was you could walk all of {in} without stopping to fight something. It isn't much to want. I'd pay to have it back.

notices.title: Father's Gloves
notices.text: My father's work gloves have hung by the clock a long while. They'd do more good on somebody's hands. See off two lots in {in} and they're yours.

thanks: Is that so. I wasn't asking, mind.
Hm. My granddad would've done it slower.
I'll remark on it to somebody. Here.

notices.title: My Bales
notices.text: Things have got into my bales in {in}. Two lots, by my count. I'm not asking. I'm saying if they were gone I'd have no more use for the rock salt.

notices.title: A Remark
notices.text: This isn't asking. There's creatures all over {in}, and if somebody cleared the lot I'd want to hear about it.

notices.title: A Hoof Pick
notices.text: Granddad's hoof pick is {where}. I know where I left it. I'm not saying I couldn't go.

notices.title: Bruised, He'll Say
notices.text: Sack of windfalls for Silas Pike. He'll say they're bruised. They are.

notices.title: Eggs, Owed
notices.got: For the lamp glass? He could've come himself. I know why he didn't.
notices.text: I owe Ada Hale for a lamp glass. Here's eggs. Mind them. I'd take them myself but she'd talk.

notices.title: For a Fence
notices.text: Wanted: two burrback quills. Don't ask. All right, it's a fence. It's for a fence.

notices.title: Father's Boots
notices.text: Clear two lots out of {in} and you can have my father's boots. Good boots. Been to Hardscrabble and back, which is more than he'd say for me.
